name: kimi-code

command.argv_notes: Evidence: the operator-local kimi job runner's buildKimiArgs (kimi-process.ts:160-181, 2026-09): print mode is `-p <prompt> --output-format stream-json`; model is `-m`; extra dirs are `--add-dir`. `-p` fixes auto permission and is mutually exclusive with --yolo/--auto/--plan (startup refusal), so no permission flag is ever passed here. Re-verified 2026-09-18 on 0.43.1 with a native kimi-protocol API-key alias: P1 write and P3 resume passed; read-only was rejected by paidan before dispatch. Native config bytes remained unchanged. Network-fetch and other permissions were not re-probed.

env._env_notes: native_default = paidan does not set the variable at all (kimi runs against the user's real home). Paidan never stages or copies kimi config.

permission.presets_notes: print mode fixes auto permission; kimi has NO native headless read-only tier (probe run 5f0d9fc2: task-mode=read-only wrote the file anyway). read-only stays unsupported until the ACP transport lane exists.

denial_evidence.via: parser detects the Moonshot provider safety-block terminal line on stderr (format evidenced by the operator-local kimi job runner's kimi-output.ts:60); not yet live-probed through paidan

permission.headless_notes: Print mode uses native auto permission; no interactive approval channel. paidan cannot enforce a read-only preset for this endpoint.

resume.notes: Evidence: the operator-local kimi job runner's kimi-process.ts:169 passes `-S <sessionId>`; the native stderr hint prints `kimi -r session_xxx` (the runner's kimi-output.ts:56, whole-line only). sessionId is extracted from the stdout meta row {role:"meta", type:"session.resume_hint", session_id} (the runner's kimi-output.ts:102-111). kimi's native session store is scoped per working directory (sessions/wd_<hash>/): a resume run must use the same cwd as the original run, else the endpoint exits non-zero (paidan probe P3, 2026-09-10). Model inheritance on resume: officially unspecified.

models.notes: Native provider list JSON, whitelisted before output/cache: real model.provider, protocol, OAuth/API type, wire model, model overrides and per-model efforts. KIMI_MODEL_NAME is shown as the native temporary alias. Explicit model/effort selections are checked against the current source without fallback. No account/quota guarantee; raw native JSON contains credentials and must never be logged.

effort.notes: No CLI effort flag; paidan passes KIMI_MODEL_THINKING_EFFORT only in the child environment. Native 0.43.1 request capture (2026-09-18): kimi protocol honored high, while openai/anthropic retained native low. Explicit paidan effort is therefore allowed only for confirmed kimi-protocol thinking models, checked against their effective supportEfforts (including overrides). A disabled optional thinking mode also refuses the override. Other protocols may select a model alias but follow native effort; changing native settings requires user consent. The option set is adapter syntax, not every model's supported levels.

parser_notes: stream-json JSONL on stdout: assistant text rows {role:"assistant", content}; session hint {role:"meta", type:"session.resume_hint", session_id, command}. Non-JSON stdout line or mid-line EOF degrades the parser (terminal judgment then cannot be exit-code-based). Evidence: the operator-local kimi job runner's kimi-output.ts:88-114.
